prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: -sent you an email about my latest experience and would appreciate a response, please. Thanks.
Delta: Hello Aliess! Thank you for reaching out to us. Did you submit a formal complaint? Did you receive a case number? (cont...)  *HKS

Customer: you sent an email yesterday with sales to London but all links were broken. Can you link me to sale https://t.co/eimKEwajek
Delta: Hey, Elise. Here are our London deals: https://t.co/T9xEVjKEal. *ASK

Customer: Tried to get access to my account too many times and denied. I sent an email using your form on the Delta site. Please help.
Delta: Hi Bob, please provide your SkyMiles number. I would like to take a look. *AJY

Customer: . as a "valued customer", you're going to take up to 30 days to respond? On vacation til then? By then I'll be back w/  https://t.co/80gKxBC3sf
Delta: ...case will be reviewed/responded and resolved.  *HAA 2/2

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: service_complaint):
"""Reminder  I recently sent you an email outlining what a nightmarish ordeal this flight was. From a valued customer...hit me back https://t.co/Sgc2LxRRrd"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Hi, could you share your SkyMiles number or case reference so we can review your recent flight experience?
